# `bin/approve`

A tool: run it from the root of an instance (or of the kit, for the kit's own tools).
Source: [`bin/approve`](../../../bin/approve)

## What it says about itself

```text
bin/approve — THE USER'S ACT. The hook keeps the orchestrator away from it.

  bin/approve RUN [RUN …] [--digest HEX] -- <launch flags>   a launch (flags required, --model included); several runs = batch consent;
                                                             flags after -- bind bin/run-external's flags
  bin/approve --ledger RUN c1 [c2 …]                         a bin/ledger-claims append of exactly these ids
  bin/approve --annotate C-NNN "text"                        a bin/annotate-claim note with exactly this text
  bin/approve --annotate-batch FILE                          several notes (a JSON list of {"id", "text"} in FILE),
                                                             one approval, printed in full; `bin/annotate-claim --batch FILE`
  bin/approve --session -- <astra-session arguments>         a headless bin/astra-session
  --show also prints every file's contents; --digest refuses unless the bytes are the ones bin/manifest showed.

Prints path, size and sha256 of everything the approval is bound to, writes a single-use record that
expires in 30 minutes, and ledgers an APPROVE line. Any later edit to those bytes voids it.
```
